about: History's own buildings (your answer 'History's own on their dates, then by need'): what a realm the computer runs builds in its year, if it still holds the province and can build there, before anything chosen by need. Each entry raises that building one level. 'building' is an id in buildings.json, 'province' a province name, 'realm' a key in realms_bc300.json. A realm that missed the year (at war, short of silver, not yet holding the place) still builds it within 'window' years (20 if not given). Sources are the ancient authors (book.chapter).

buildings.name: the Via Appia
buildings.why: Appius Claudius the censor paved the road from Rome to Capua.

buildings.name: the Aqua Appia
buildings.why: Rome's first aqueduct, built by the same censor.

buildings.name: the silver mint
buildings.why: Rome began striking silver coin of its own.

buildings.name: the Anio Vetus
buildings.why: Paid for from the spoils of the war with Pyrrhus.

buildings.name: the Via Flaminia
buildings.why: Gaius Flaminius ran a road across the Apennines to the Adriatic.

buildings.name: the first public library
buildings.why: Asinius Pollio opened Rome's first public library from the spoils of Illyria.

buildings.name: the Baths of Agrippa
buildings.why: The first great public baths of Rome.

buildings.name: Portus
buildings.why: Claudius built a new harbour at Ostia for the grain ships.

buildings.name: the Aurelian Walls
buildings.why: Aurelian walled Rome again against the barbarian raids.

buildings.name: the Museum and Library of Alexandria
buildings.why: Ptolemy I gathered scholars and books in Alexandria.

buildings.name: the Great Harbour and the Heptastadion
buildings.why: A mole to the island of Pharos made Alexandria's twin harbours.

buildings.name: the draining of the Fayum
buildings.why: Ptolemy II drained the lake's edge and settled his soldiers on the new land.

buildings.name: the markets of Alexandria
buildings.why: The city of Alexander grew into the greatest market of the age.

buildings.name: Antioch on the Orontes
buildings.why: Seleucus founded Antioch and the cities of the Syrian tetrapolis.

buildings.name: Seleucia on the Tigris
buildings.why: Seleucus' eastern capital drew the trade and people of Babylon.

buildings.name: the Cothon
buildings.why: Carthage's round war harbour, with sheds for 220 ships.

buildings.name: the Syracusia
buildings.why: Hieron II had Archimedes oversee the building of the greatest ship of the age.

buildings.name: the great theatre
buildings.why: Hieron II enlarged the theatre cut in the rock.
buildings.source: Diodorus 16.83; its inscriptions to Queen Philistis
